positions.as_written: Take the history: the age, the sport, how long the pain has been present, and whether it is worse during or after activity.
Ask specifically about catching, locking and giving way, since those are the clinical markers of an unstable fragment.
Assess the effusion, because a recurrent effusion after sport is often the only objective finding.
Measure the range and note any block or any pain at a particular angle.
Assess the gait, since a child with a condylar lesion may walk with the limb externally rotated.
Examine the other knee, because the lesion is bilateral in a proportion of cases.
